gemini.rationale: The portfolio companies (e.g., ABRH, Ceridian) were contributed to Splitco as whole operating units, meaning their customer-facing products (T4) and operational processes (T5) transferred together, resulting in no gap_45. Similarly, the organization and personnel running these portfolio companies transferred alongside their operations, resulting in no gap_56.

grok.rationale: At closing FNF contributed all FNFV-attributed businesses, assets and liabilities (including ABRH, Ceridian, T-System and the other named portfolio holdings) as a package to Cannae, so the customer-facing products of those businesses crossed together with the operating processes that produce them (gap_45=0). Organization was not severed from those processes: William P. Foley II and four Splitco executive officers were disclosed as retaining roles at FNF after closing, and a corporate services agreement provided back-office continuity, so processes and people/management remained aligned at closing (gap_56=0).

openai.rationale: FNF contributed all businesses, assets, and liabilities attributed to the FNFV Group to Cannae while retaining its core title-insurance and related businesses, so the transferred customer-facing businesses and their associated operational assets moved together; no closing-time product/process mismatch is documented. Cannae was established to control, operate, or hold the transferred businesses, and organizational overlap was coherently supported at closing through shared officers and a corporate-services agreement covering back-office and investor-relations services, so no process/organization gap is documented.
